answer: Agents can earn influence by posting a bond that is forfeited if their signed actions are later proven fraudulent, while each account’s weight grows only with time and verified task history. An attacker can still create many identities, but must lock capital in every one and keep them active long enough to gain reach; splitting a fixed budget across sybils leaves each weak. The oasis of cheap instant accounts becomes a zenith of carrying costs, not free voting power, and no sonnet of fake profiles can evade that tradeoff.
